slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will pull you
out of your dopamine addiction

long walks with no input

walk for thirty minutes with no music, podcast or phone. the first ten minutes feel boring, then your brain starts producing its own ideas again. the more you practise it, the more natural it becomes.

working with your hands

do a puzzle, a crossword or a small model in the evening instead of scrolling. slow rewards slowly teach your brain to enjoy patience again. it's a small change with a surprisingly big effect.

one thing timer

set a twenty five minute timer and do one single thing with your phone in another room. the urge to check it fades faster than you'd expect. try it for one week and notice the difference.

swapping the scroll

every time you open social media, learn one real thing instead: a space fact, a piece of history. most people never think about it, which is exactly why it works.
slides.texte_sophia:
swapping the scroll

every time i reach for the feed, i learn one real thing instead. the Sophia app turns it into one short lesson a day, and real curiosity slowly replaced the scroll.

slides.texte_overlay:
growing a plant

grow a plant from a seed and look after it daily. waiting weeks to see something grow is the perfect antidote to instant gratification. it sounds simple, but very few people actually do it.
